changes.before: Write badge(name): trim outside spaces and return "Hello, " plus the name. For an empty or spaces-only name, return "Hello, guest". Keep spaces inside the name.
changes.after: Remove spaces around a name and use a guest greeting when nothing remains.

before: A name typed into a form can contain extra spaces. A string is text. This project changes how that text is displayed without changing the original input. You already know functions and conditions; now you will combine them with a string method, an action attached to a text value.

Calling trim() removes whitespace from both ends of a string. Whitespace includes spaces and line breaks. The dot selects the method; parentheses call it. It does not squeeze spaces inside a name or change capital letters. Store the returned string, because JavaScript strings are not edited in place.

An empty string is written "". After trimming, compare the result with "" using ===. That comparison produces true or false. Decide on your fallback after cleanup, or a string containing only spaces could accidentally become a blank badge.

The plus sign joins strings here. Both "Hello, " and a cleaned name are strings. Keep the comma and one space in the greeting. This function accepts strings only; accepting numbers or objects would need a separate decision about validation. Do not silently change someone's name to a different capitalization.

Write badge(name) and keep it reusable: checks call it with different names, spaces and an empty string. Try a name containing two words. Predict which spaces should remain before running it. The checks examine returned values, so displaying a greeting with console.log alone does not complete the function.
after:
A typed name may have extra spaces at its ends. Use a string method, an action attached to text, to clean them up.

Return the cleaned greeting without changing the original input.

`trim()` removes whitespace from both ends. Whitespace includes spaces, tabs, and line breaks.

It keeps spaces inside the name and leaves capital letters alone. Save its returned string; it does not edit the original string.

`""` is an empty string. After trimming, compare with `""` to see whether any text remains.

Check after cleanup so a spaces-only name does not become a blank badge.

`+` joins strings here. Keep the comma and one space in `"Hello, "`.

This function accepts text. Keep the person's letter case and spaces inside their name.

Write `badge(name)` to return the greeting for each supplied name. Empty or whitespace-only text should give `"Hello, guest"`.

The checks use returned text. Printing alone does not return the answer.

headings: Clean the edges of a typed name
Check for empty text after cleaning
Join the greeting and cleaned name
Return a greeting for each input

project.title: A tidy name badge
project.task: Return `"Hello, "` plus the trimmed name. If no text remains, return `"Hello, guest"`. Keep inside spaces and letter case.
project.done_when: Names, empty text, and whitespace-only text give the expected greetings.
